children: said on Tuesday it would simplify its ownership structure by buying out a stake from its top shareholder, after it reported adjusted full-year core earnings in line with market expectations.

The company has agreed to acquire the Mankel family's 47.5% stake in its operating business for 2.13 billion Swiss francs ($2.63 billion), to be settled through an issuance of about 36.2 million new shares in the listed entity and a cash payment of 29.9 million francs.

The Mankel family, the former owners of Dorma before its merger with Kaba, already owns 10.8% in the SIX-listed Dormakaba Holding AG, on top of the stake in the operating business which is held through an intermediate holding company in Germany.
"The proposed new setup will remove inefficiencies and give the company greater financial flexibility," Dormakaba Chair Svein Richard Brandtzæg said.
The transaction is subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, as well as other customary closing conditions. Dormakaba expects to close the deal on or around January 7, 2027.

The company's adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation were 449 million francs in the 2025/26 financial year, which met analysts' average estimate provided by the company.

For the newly started fiscal year, Dormakaba expects organic sales growth of around 3%, matching last year's pace. It expects its adjusted core profit margin to exceed 11%, down from the 16.1% it reported for last year.
